A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PRIMAL and contain readable main texts and complete supplements. Methods, equations, tables and figures can be matched across revisions, including material moved into the appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original motion-generation, responsiveness, adaptation, ablation, runtime and perceptual-study results in Tables 1–3 and A2–A6.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a controlled ballet-generation and walking-to-ballet experiment in Section 7.1 and Figure A1.

M1.justification: The proposed denoisers, training losses, impulse and CBG control, inference processing and ControlNet adaptor remain unchanged. AdaLN moves to the supplement rather than being removed. Cross-attention in the new controlled experiment is an experimental configuration, not a replacement of the main method.

E1.justification: Section 7.1 adds ballet-only training and an explicit walking-to-ballet generalization scenario. The existing AMASS training subsets, HumanEva/SFU evaluations, personalized action classes and target-reaching tasks are retained.

E2.justification: The new ballet experiment adds a controlled comparison against an otherwise matched model generating 40 frames from 20 history frames, versus 15 from one. Existing named benchmark comparators remain unchanged. InsActor is newly discussed and cited, but not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: The added study overfits models to a 229-frame ballet sequence, evaluates 780-frame continuation and 156-frame generation initialized from walking, and specifies cross-attention for multiframe conditioning. These are new experimental settings; the retained benchmark and user-study protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 7.1 and Figure A1 add a focused diagnostic comparison testing long-term stability and transfer from walking after ballet-only training. It probes the combined history/horizon design. Existing architecture, noise, activation, dimension and post-processing ablations are retained.

E5.justification: No repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests are added. Perceptual-study sampling and filtering remain unchanged, and the new ballet results use point estimates.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–3 and A1–A6 are unchanged. Section 7.1 newly reports ASR of 0.08 versus 0.12 for ballet continuation and 0.06 versus 0.30 for walking-initialized generation, alongside qualitative stability and transition findings.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(8), the motion-state representation, losses and conditional-generation formulation are retained. The new generalization and physical-realism discussions introduce no mathematical derivations, formal assumptions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion temper the framing from learning motion dynamics and emergent physics for embodied intelligence toward mimicking body movement for interactive avatars. Claims of two-stage learning, real-time control, responsiveness and effective adaptation remain.

C2.justification: Sections 6 and 7.3 explicitly distinguish perceptually plausible motion from guaranteed physical realism, extending v1's existing acknowledgment of nonphysical failures. New discussion interprets the ballet results as generalization evidence and argues that hierarchical simulation adds overhead and limits responsiveness.

D1.justification: Section 7.1 documents cross-attention conditioning for the new controlled study. Core hyperparameters, hardware, training time and the project link remain unchanged. The introduction's explicit research-release statement covering the Unreal demo is omitted, without establishing that access was withdrawn.

R1.justification: v2 adds InsActor and expands positioning against hierarchical diffusion-and-simulation approaches in Sections 2 and 7.2. It removes the biological motor-primitives motivation and the Mussa-Ivaldi–Bizzi citation. Most related-work coverage remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract is rewritten, introductory terminology and explanations are revised, and a discussion section is inserted before the renumbered supplement. Detailed architecture exposition moves into the supplement; the main section sequence and most technical and experimental prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the ballet visualization as Figure A1, simplifies main Figure 2 to InContext, and retains the original two-architecture diagram as Figure A2. Existing control and user-study figures move and are renumbered; tables receive best-score highlighting and some relocation.

improvement.justification: v2 more clearly aligns its physical-realism claims with perceptual evidence and adds a targeted generalization check in Section 7.1. These improve calibration and support for the design while retaining the original results. The added experiment uses one ballet training sequence and changes history and prediction horizons together, so its evidential gain is limited.
